topic.title: Index of Errors
topic.p: This index lists every numbered Workflow compiler diagnostic, including RPC and C++ generation errors. A code can have several messages; all message templates are listed under that code. Words in braces, such as {type}, are filled in by the compiler. {candidates} can span several lines. Message spelling and punctuation follow the compiler.

Examples are intentionally invalid. Unless a context is stated, each code block is a complete module. An example may produce more than one diagnostic. Links beside examples lead to the corresponding compiler test or implementation. Runtime exceptions are separate from these compile-time diagnostics.
The numbered messages are defined in WfAnalyzer_Errors.cpp. The compiler reports a source location together with each message.

topic.title: Parser errors without a code
topic.p: Lexical and grammatical errors occur before semantic analysis and have no numbered Workflow code. The following messages come from the shared parser.

topic.p: Example: # outside a string or comment is not a Workflow token.

topic.title: D5: Ambiguous interface implementation

program.code: D5: Cannot decide which function to implement in multiple targets:{candidates}.

topic.p: Example context: native reflection exposes two distinct methods named Run with the same func():void signature on one interface. A new interface expression with override func Run():void {} cannot choose which reflected method to implement. This diagnostic is checked after matching both the name and the complete function type; ordinary Workflow duplicate declarations can be rejected earlier.

topic.title: H9: Duplicate generated RPC name

program.code: H9: RPC generated {category} name "{generatedName}" is duplicated.

topic.p: Example context: generated RPC metadata attempts to insert two event entries with the same full name, such as Service.Changed. The second entry is rejected. The same check covers generated type and method names. This is a metadata-generation consistency check; ordinary source-level duplicates may be rejected before this stage.

topic.title: I0: Missing RPC property mode

program.code: I0: RPC wrapper generation requires property "{member}" to have @rpc:Cached or @rpc:Dynamic.

topic.p: Example context: an RPC wrapper generator receives an interface property named Service.Count with neither @rpc:Cached nor @rpc:Dynamic in its metadata. Normal RPC analysis supplies a default property mode before wrapper generation; this error identifies incomplete generator input, rather than requiring every source property to write the default explicitly.

topic.title: I1: Missing RPC return transfer mode

program.code: I1: RPC wrapper generation requires method "{member}" to have @rpc:Byval or @rpc:Byref on its collection return value.

topic.p: Example context: wrapper input contains func Read():int[] without either @rpc:Byval or @rpc:Byref on its return value. Normal RPC analysis adds the default transfer mode before this stage; manually supplied or modified metadata must preserve it.

topic.title: I2: Missing RPC parameter transfer mode

program.code: I2: RPC wrapper generation requires parameter "{member}" to have @rpc:Byval or @rpc:Byref because it is a collection parameter.

topic.p: Example context: wrapper input contains func Write(values:int[]):void without either @rpc:Byval or @rpc:Byref on values. Normal RPC analysis adds the default transfer mode before this stage; manually supplied or modified metadata must preserve it.

topic.title: I3: Ambiguous generated RPC identifier

program.code: I3: RPC mangled name "{identifier}" is ambiguous between "{previousName}" and "{currentName}".

topic.p: During RPC wrapper generation, the distinct full names A::B and A__B both become the identifier A__B. Avoid names that collide after :: becomes __ and punctuation in generated member names becomes _.

topic.title: J1: Invalid variant expression

program.code: CPP1: (C++ Code Generation) Cannot decide order of the following classes. It is probably caused by inheritance relationships of internal classes inside these classes:{candidates}.

topic.p: This error appears when generating C++, after ordinary Workflow analysis succeeds.

topic.title: CPP2: Incompatible C++ file grouping

program.code: CPP2: (C++ Code Generation) @cpp:File atrribute values for these classes are invalid. Generating classes to source files specified by these attribute values will create source files which do not compile. It is probably caused by inheritance relationships of internal classes inside these classes:{candidates}.

topic.p: This error appears when generating C++. The two declarations assigned to Custom cannot be emitted together around the intervening base class.
